USBC: named players in SDs beyond luck (players.py); human tables plus Stu boards beat human tables alone by +0.71

norm_avg.py's expectations become a function that players.py reuses. players.py measures named players on their
adult boards against every adult player with 20+ boards in the role, in units of the field's skill spread (SD
beyond luck, with a bootstrap error), raw and shrunk by reliability. The from-scratch nets at full size: both sets
together beat the human tables alone by +0.71 +- 0.08 over 4,000 deals (nets alone).

These are scoped Stu research reports, not a complete full-hash/training-family proof or general collector/GenX actor replacement. R3 BEN baseline -0.09+-0.09 on2047deals is a dated peer result, not an owned stop/self-play gate. players.py normalizes human-player reports and splits years; arena scoring unchanged. Retain strict792c4cb Gen8 actors, immutable current corpus/exclusions, three normal/zero BEN and original guards. No new model/source/settings/worker change, local training/import, gate, self-play, promotion or peer operation. Any future new cohort requires complete pinned training-family membership of ALL released models, including actual R4 human/bot/arena/replay inputs; current original bytes/proofs stay unchanged.
